content: 1. Therapy with lumacaftor/ivacaftor should be closely monitored due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A. At steady-state, the net exposure of ivacaftor is not expected to exceed the levels observed when ivacaftor is administered alone at the approved dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. Therefore, no dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, the dose should be reduced to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, the recommended daily dose can be resumed. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 2. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the dose of lumateperone should be reduced to 5 mg/day. 3. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The dose of maraviroc should be reduced to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Indinavir also increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of marijuana through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may necessitate a reduced mavacamten dose. 7. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Mavorixafor also increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Co-administration of mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, with a sensitive P-gp substrate may lead to serious adverse effects due to minimal substrate concentration changes. 8. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Indinavir increases meperidine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required due to the potential for increased toxicity. 10. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Indinavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors should be considered. 12. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 14. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 16. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Indinavir and mifepristone both increase each other's levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Mifepristone increases indinavir levels through the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 18. Indinavir decreases the effects of miglitol through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors should be considered. 19. Indinavir and mipomersen both have the potential to increase each other's toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. Both drugs may elevate hepatic enzymes; liver function tests should be monitored. 20. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are required. 22. Mitotane decreases the levels of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; dosage adjustments may be necessary when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 23. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of modafinil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 24. Indinavir increases the levels of mometasone (inhaled) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required due to the potential for increased toxicity, including the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 25. Indinavir increases the levels of mometasone (intranasal) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 26. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Indinavir increases the levels of naldemedine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Adverse effects should be monitored if co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Indinavir decreases the effects of nateglinide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors should be considered. 29. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 31. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is necessary. 33. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Indinavir also increases nevirapine levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required. 34. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nicardipine also increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Initiate nifedipine at the lowest dose available if given concomitantly. Nifedipine also decreases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 36. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nilotinib also increases indinavir levels through the same mechanism. Indinavir further increases nilotinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 37. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events with concomitant use. 38. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 39. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are required. 41. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 42. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 43. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 44. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease ondansetron clearance. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 45. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are required. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 46. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat, a CYP3A4 substrate, by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 47. Indinavir increases the levels of ospemifene by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 48. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 50. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel protein-bound by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 51. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 52. Indinavir increases the levels of panobinostat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 53. Indinavir increases the levels of paricalcitol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required due to the potential for increased toxicity. 54. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 55. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of perampanel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 57. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 58. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 59. Indinavir increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are required. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 60. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 61. Ponatinib increases the levels of indinavir by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 62. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required.
